faq.a: The issue price is the fixed price per share at which a company offers its shares to the public during an IPO.

faq.q: What is the difference between Mainboard and SME IPOs?
faq.a: Mainboard IPOs are for larger, more established companies that list on the main exchanges (NSE, BSE). SME (Small and Medium Enterprises) IPOs are for smaller companies, listed on dedicated SME platforms, often with different rules and lower minimum investment amounts.

faq.q: How do I calculate my return if I was allotted shares?
faq.a: You can calculate your return by taking the current market price, subtracting your IPO issue price, dividing by the IPO issue price, and then multiplying by 100 to get a percentage.

faq.q: Should I sell my shares on listing day if there's a gain?
faq.a: Whether to sell on listing day or hold depends on your personal financial goals and risk tolerance. Some investors aim for quick listing gains, while others prefer to hold for the long term, believing in the company's growth potential.

faq.q: Is it too late to invest if an IPO has already listed?
faq.a: No, once an IPO lists, its shares can be bought and sold on the open market just like any other stock. You can invest in a listed company at any time, subject to market conditions and your own research.
